summary: Peter Adamson is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Williams College (~1990–1994) and the University of Notre Dame (~1994–2001). He held posts at King's College London (~2000–2012) and the University of Munich (~2012).

Peter Alan Roberts works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed doctoral studies under supervisors Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

Peter C. Bisschop works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Groningen in 2004 under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson, and later held posts at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010) and Leiden University (2010).
Peter Connolly works in religious studies and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at Lancaster University and became a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied at Yale University and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under traditional teachers Seungsahn Haengwon and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim. He held leadership posts at the East-West Center.
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche and advisers N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch. He held a post at Deakin University.

Peter Francis Kornicki works in Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oxford, Tokyo University of Education, and under Masamichi Asukai and Mitsukuni Yoshida, he held posts at the University of Tasmania (1978–1982), Kyoto University (~1982–1985), and Cambridge (~1985).

Peter Friedlander is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (1983–1991). He held an associate professor post at the Australian National University in 2013.

Peter Gaeffke worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Regensburg, Mainz (PhD 1952), and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies, later serving as professor at Utrecht University (1965–1975) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003).
Peter Gerlitz was a religious studies scholar who studied under Friedrich Heiler (~1948–1954). He held a post at the University of Bremen from ~1973 to 1991.

Peter Giles was a linguist who studied at King's College London, Aberdeen, Cambridge, Freiburg, and Leipzig under teachers John Peile and Karl Brugmann. He held posts at Emmanuel College (1887, 1911) and the University of Cambridge (Reader in Comparative Philology, 1891).

Peter Gyallay-Pap is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the London School of Economics by 1990. He held an adjunct post at Adams State University, attested in 2007.

Peter Hartmann worked in linguistics, Indology, and Japanology, earning his PhD at Münster (1948–1950) under Alfred Schmitt. He held professorships at the University of Münster (1956) and the University of Konstanz (1969).

Peter Harvey is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996 and held a post at the University of Sunderland from 1976 to 2011, becoming Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies.
Peter Haskel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who pursued graduate studies at Columbia University under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson earned his PhD at Yale University (~1956–1961). He taught at Yale (~1961–1963), Vassar College, the University of Washington (~1963–1970), Bennington College (~1968–1971), and the University of Otago (~1971–1998).

Peter James Gilks is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and completed a PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers, alongside several traditional Tibetan teachers.

Peter K. Austin is a linguist who earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1975–1978). He served as Foundation Professor in Linguistics at the University of Melbourne (1996–2002) and professor at SOAS University of London (2002–2018).

Peter Koret is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London. He has held academic posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.
